headline: Apple unveils third generation of Apple Foundation Models with on-device and cloud AI
summary: Apple's WWDC26 keynote detailed its latest AI advancements, including on-device processing and enhanced cloud capabilities for its new Foundation Models.
details: During WWDC26, Apple announced the third generation of its Apple Foundation Models (AFM). This new iteration focuses on integrating AI capabilities more deeply across its ecosystem, offering both on-device processing for privacy and speed, and cloud-based solutions for more complex tasks.

The on-device AI features leverage the power of Apple's latest hardware, allowing for faster response times and enhanced user privacy as sensitive data does not need to leave the device. This approach is crucial for features like real-time language translation and personalized content suggestions.

For more demanding AI tasks, Apple is also enhancing its cloud-based AI infrastructure. This allows users to access more powerful AI models and capabilities without requiring high-end hardware, ensuring a consistent experience across all Apple devices.

The announcement also included details on visionOS 27, iOS 27, and macOS 27, all of which will feature significant AI-driven enhancements. Design resources for these upcoming operating systems are now available to developers.

headline_marked: Apple's iOS 27 [[generative AI tools]] expand photos with fake pixels
headline: Apple's iOS 27 generative AI tools expand photos with fake pixels
summary: New 'Extend' and 'Spatial Reframe' features in iOS 27 allow users to add space or change perspective in photos, generating new pixels.
details: Apple is introducing new generative AI features to its Photos app in iOS 27, aiming to enhance user creativity while maintaining a measured approach. Unlike competitors, Apple emphasizes that its AI tools are not just for the sake of AI but are designed to solve specific photographic challenges.

The upcoming iOS 27 will feature two new AI-powered tools: 'Extend' and 'Spatial Reframe'. 'Extend' allows users to expand the canvas of a photo by up to 25%, generating plausible background pixels. 'Spatial Reframe' enables users to alter the perspective of an image, also by generating new pixels.

According to Jon McCormack, Apple's camera chief, these tools aim to give 'normal people these absolute superpowers' by simplifying complex editing tasks. The AI 'thinks' about what should be in the expanded or reframed image and generates it, making advanced editing accessible.

Apple is implementing restrictions to prevent misuse. The 'Extend' feature only works once per image, and generated pixels are limited to the background, not altering the main subject's face. The 'Clean Up' tool also prevents the removal of the primary subject.

To ensure transparency, Apple will integrate Google DeepMind's SynthID technology later this year. This will add an invisible watermark to AI-edited images, allowing platforms to flag them as generated content, though the effectiveness of such watermarks is debated.

McCormack stressed Apple's commitment to the authenticity of photography, viewing it as a way to preserve personal memories. The company aims to provide tools that enhance these memories without compromising the integrity of the captured moment, contrasting with approaches that allow more extensive image manipulation.

Della Huff, product manager for Camera and Photos software, stated that the AI models were trained to minimize 'hallucinations' and avoid generating elements that are not plausible within the context of the original photo. If an element is not needed, the AI will not create it.
